ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 9-7-1 so far, winners of four straight.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they pounce on turnovers and hit everything that moves.
Their goaltending has let them down.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 12-4-1 so far, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 8-5-3 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and rarely block shots.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The rebuild grinds on in Calgary: no playoffs in four seasons, and a 7-9-1 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they settle for a lot of hopeful shots and play fast, wide-open games.
Their power play has no bite and they spend a lot of time in the box.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 13-3-2 out of the gate.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 16 of their 18 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 4-12-1 start, losers of five straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They rarely block shots and spend a lot of the night in their own end.
Their power play has no bite.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: The Avalanche, playoff regulars, are 9-6-2 so far.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Night to night, they shoot from distance and play fast, wide-open games.
Their penalty kill is airtight.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The Blue Jackets are 7-8-0, still looking for their first playoff spot in six seasons.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
On the ice, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get a lot of their shots blocked.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars are 9-5-2, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get in front of a lot of shots and grind games down.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The Red Wings are 7-7-3, still looking for their first playoff spot in ten seasons.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and leave most of the shooting to the forwards.
They stay out of the box and their power play is lethal.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 11-3-3, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they lean hard on their top players and send their defensemen in to shoot.
Their power play is lethal.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers have bounced back to 9-5-2.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in nine of their 16 games.
Night to night, they hound the puck in the other team’s end and give up very few shots.
Their penalty kill is airtight and their power play is lethal.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 5-7-2 this time.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to leave most of the shooting to the forwards and keep the other team to hopeful shots.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 12-3-3 so far, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in ten of their 18 games.
Night to night, they crash the net for second chances and get pinned in their own end on long shifts.
They stay out of the box and their goaltending has been stealing games.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 10-3-3 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up dangerous chances.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators are 7-4-5, winners of three straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and let the other team shoot a lot.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils have bounced back to 11-5-0, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 14 of their 16 games.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders are 7-6-2.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their penalty kill leaks.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers are 9-7-1.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get a lot of their shots blocked and get right to the net.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 10-6-1 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
They stay out of the box.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 4-10-4 so far.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They grind games down and get a lot of their shots blocked.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 5-9-2 so far, losers of four straight.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Their game? They get right to the net and sit back rather than forecheck.
They create chances even when shorthanded.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The rebuild grinds on in San Jose: no playoffs in seven seasons, and a 7-10-1 start, losers of four straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and shoot from distance.
Their power play has no bite and their penalty kill leaks.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: Could this be the year? The Kraken haven’t made the playoffs in three seasons, but they’re 9-5-1 so far.
Don’t get too comfortable, though: they’ve been outchanced in most of those games, and that tends to catch up with a team.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their penalty kill leaks and their power play has no bite.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 7-7-2.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and get to the dangerous chances.
Their power play has no bite.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 10-3-2, and in the mix again.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in ten of their 15 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and get into a lot of chippy games.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Maple Leafs are 8-7-2.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
They spend a lot of time in the box and their goaltending has let them down.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 10-6-1 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 15 of their 17 games.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and collapse around the net and give up the point.
Their goaltending has let them down.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 3-14-1, losers of four straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Expect them to spend a lot of the night in their own end and crash the net for second chances.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 11-5-2.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in 13 of their 18 games.
Expect them to keep the other team to hopeful shots and get in front of a lot of shots.
They stay out of the box and their penalty kill is airtight.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals are 8-6-0.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They get to the dangerous chances and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: Last season was one to forget in Winnipeg, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 6-8-3.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely block shots.
They create chances even when shorthanded, but their penalty kill leaks.
